Equiv only constrains step behaviour, which the opaque value does not see, and the statement has no IteratorLoop binder, so the two-loop trick that decided forIn/fold/foldM/drain/toExt*Set does not apply; two instantiations of T' sharing the opaque term have Equiv (hence equal-valued) finite partners, so no diagonal argument exists. Model argument: interpreting opaqueFix R F a as the well-founded fixpoint on the R-accessible part (default elsewhere) makes T' true, since an iterator Equiv to a finite one is accessible and the library's step induction goes through; interpreting the value at SL state 1 as anything but [0] makes T' false. Lean support: the support lemma derives ¬T' from S1.toList ≠ F1.toList (resp. toArray/toListRev; SL state 1 is Equiv to the finite FN state 1, W19c3.eqv/eqvM).

Equiv only constrains step behaviour, which the opaque value does not see, and the statement has no IteratorLoop binder, so the two-loop trick that decided forIn/fold/foldM/drain/toExt*Set does not apply; two instantiations of T' sharing the opaque term have Equiv (hence equal-valued) finite partners, so no diagonal argument exists. Model argument: interpreting opaqueFix R F a as the well-founded fixpoint on the R-accessible part (default elsewhere) makes T' true, since an iterator Equiv to a finite one is accessible and the library's step induction goes through; interpreting the value at SL state 1 as anything but [0] makes T' false. Lean support: the support lemma derives ¬T' from S1.toList ≠ F1.toList (resp. toArray/toListRev; SL state 1 is Equiv to the finite FN state 1, W19c3.eqv/eqvM).

reason: independent (opaque fixpoint): without the dropped Productive instance the Zip type (and Take of Zip) is not well-founded, so the left side is an opaqueFix value of the zip consumer, and the right side combines opaqueFix values of the non-productive component (its atIdxSlow?/toList or that of its take) at different arguments; no equation links them, and the remaining Finite/Productive side cannot force a value (the opaque-length trick needs an evaluable side).
